## Electronic screening and optical excitations

Use benzene to establish the screening calculations, then compare B3LYP and DD-DFT for benzene and the difluoroboron dyes.

::: {.molecules}
![](../../private/research-findings/projects/2026-10-21_164930/figures/benzene.svg){width=73px .molecule} ![](../../private/research-findings/projects/2026-10-21_164930/figures/methoxy-chelate.svg){width=405px .molecule}
:::


| Status | Period | Project | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ![In progress](../../private/research-findings/projects/icons/hourglass.svg "In progress"){.workflow-status} | 17–30 Oct 2026 | [Molecular screening $\varepsilon_s$ and $S_0\rightarrow S_n$ excitations](2026-10-21_164930/) | Connects Gaussian geometries and excitations with Lotus screening and BLYP-based DD-DFT weights. |

::: {.link-detail data-href="2026-10-21_164930/"}
::: {.callout-note .status-in-progress title="In progress"}
The B3LYP results of both checkpoint-chained workflows are suspect, so the comparison is being rebuilt without checkpoint reuse; the benzene rebuild reproduces the checkpoint-chained spectra within $3\,\mathrm{meV}$ and reaches self-consistent DD-DFT weights after a second geometry/screening cycle, and the methoxy rebuild is prepared; the checkpoint-chained dimethylamino workflow is superseded before submission.
:::
